subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Salience of Tax Burden
description: A 60-second lesson on Salience of Tax Burden.

hook.text: A store posts prices without sales tax. You see $10 and pay $10.80. Chetty showed that making tax visible at the shelf.

buildup.text: Tax salience determines how much taxes influence behavior. If taxes are hidden or separated from prices, people.

discovery.text: Finkelstein found that when tolls switched from cash to electronic, drivers barely noticed increases.

twist.text: Governments benefit from low salience. Income tax withheld from paychecks feels smaller than writing a single annual.

climax.text: Tax transparency isn't about honesty. When citizens feel taxes, they scrutinize government spending more.

punchline.text: Taxes you do not see are taxes you do not question.

quiz.question: What did Chetty's study show about tax-inclusive pricing?
options: Making tax visible at the shelf had no effect on purchases
Making tax visible reduced purchases by 8%
Consumers preferred stores with hidden taxes
